questions.stem: According to industry practice for hand tool inspection, when should a welder remove a striking tool (chipping hammer, ball-peen) from service?

choices.A: Only when the head is loose on the handle
choices.B: Once per year regardless of condition
choices.C: When the striking face is mushroomed, chipped, or cracked
choices.D: Only when directed by a supervisor

questions.explanation: A mushroomed, chipped, or cracked striking face can shed metal shards on impact — a leading cause of eye injury. RSOS A-1.01 requires identifying worn, damaged, and defective tools and removing them from service. A loose head (A) is also a defect but not the only trigger; annual (B) and supervisor-directed (D) inspection alone are not sufficient.

sources.ref: A-1.01.03P identify worn, damaged and defective tools

questions.stem: A welder needs to measure a 3/16" root opening on a groove weld. Which measuring tool is most appropriate?

choices.A: A 12" combination square
choices.B: A framing square
choices.C: A dial caliper
choices.D: A gap gauge (welding fillet/groove gauge)

questions.explanation: A welding gap/fillet gauge is designed for exactly this measurement and is the standard shop tool for root opening and fillet leg length. A combination square (A) and framing square (B) cannot fit into a groove root. A dial caliper (C) can measure it but is fragile in a welding environment and slower to use than the purpose-built gauge.

sources.ref: A-1.01.01P select and use tools and equipment

questions.stem: What is the correct procedure for storing steel measuring tapes and machinist rules to preserve accuracy?

choices.A: Clean, lightly oil, and store in a dry location protected from impact
choices.B: Store loose in the bottom of the tool box
choices.C: Store submerged in cutting fluid
choices.D: Store outdoors to allow temperature stabilization

questions.explanation: Precision measuring tools must be cleaned, lightly oiled to prevent corrosion, and stored where they cannot be dented or bent. Loose storage (B) leads to edge damage. Cutting fluid (C) will corrode the etched markings. Outdoor storage (D) exposes tools to moisture and temperature swings that degrade accuracy.

questions.stem: A grinder's disc wobbles slightly when spinning but appears undamaged. What is the correct next action?

choices.A: Continue using — a slight wobble is normal
choices.B: Tighten the retaining nut harder until wobble stops
choices.C: Remove the disc, inspect the disc, backing flanges, and spindle for damage or debris, and replace any damaged component
choices.D: Reduce grinder RPM and continue using

questions.explanation: Wobble is never normal — it indicates a damaged disc, contaminated or worn flanges, a bent spindle, or an improperly seated disc. Any of these can cause the disc to shatter at speed. Over-tightening (B) can crack the disc. Continued use (A) or reduced RPM (D) leaves an unsafe condition. RSOS A-1.02 requires maintaining power tools per manufacturer's specifications.

questions.stem: What information on a grinding wheel label must a welder verify before mounting the wheel on a portable angle grinder?

choices.A: Maximum RPM rating equal to or greater than the grinder's rated RPM
choices.B: Only the abrasive type
choices.C: Only the diameter
choices.D: Only the manufacturer's colour code

questions.explanation: A grinding wheel must be rated for at least the grinder's maximum RPM; running a wheel above its rated speed can cause it to burst. Diameter, abrasive type, and arbor size all matter too but the RPM rating is the single most safety-critical value to verify. CSA W117.2 and OSHA/ANSI B7.1 all require this check.

questions.stem: A welder finds that a SMAW power source shows an intermittent output — the arc extinguishes randomly under load. After confirming electrode and ground connections are tight, what is the next reasonable maintenance step?

choices.A: Increase the amperage setting
choices.B: Change to a smaller electrode
choices.C: Replace the machine
choices.D: Inspect and clean electrical connections inside the machine (lockout/tagout first), check the work lead clamp and power cable for damage

questions.explanation: Intermittent output almost always traces to a loose or dirty electrical connection, damaged cables, or a worn work-lead clamp. After external checks pass, the next step is internal inspection — always with the machine locked out and tagged out first. Increasing amperage (A) or downsizing the electrode (B) masks the fault. Replacement (C) is premature.

questions.stem: When performing routine maintenance on a GTAW torch, which component is inspected for pitting and contamination and replaced when the flow-cooling passage or gas passage is restricted?

choices.A: Foot pedal
choices.B: Torch body / collet body assembly
choices.C: Power source contactor
choices.D: Regulator

questions.explanation: The GTAW torch body and collet body carry both gas flow and, on water-cooled torches, cooling water. Restrictions cause overheating and gas coverage problems. Foot pedal (A), contactor (C), and regulator (D) are separate assemblies with different failure modes.

questions.stem: A GMAW wire feeder is delivering wire erratically — surging and stubbing. Drive rolls are the correct size for the wire, and tension appears set correctly. What is the next likely cause to check?

choices.A: The shielding gas cylinder is empty
choices.B: A worn or kinked liner in the gun cable causing high feed resistance
choices.C: The power source is on the wrong polarity
choices.D: The wire spool is too new

questions.explanation: Erratic wire feed with correct roll size and tension is almost always a liner problem — worn, kinked, contaminated, or wrong-sized for the wire. Empty gas (A) causes porosity, not feed problems. Wrong polarity (C) affects arc characteristics. Spool age (D) is irrelevant if the wire is clean.

questions.stem: Which log or record is typically maintained for shop cranes, slings, and rigging hardware?

choices.A: Personal PPE log only
choices.B: Purchase price log
choices.C: Periodic inspection log with date, inspector, condition, and any defects found
choices.D: No log is required by code

questions.explanation: CSA B335 (mobile equipment) and ASME B30 series require documented periodic inspections of lifting equipment. Records include date, inspector, condition, and defects. Purchase price (B) is a business record, not a safety one. No-log (D) is incorrect — inspection records are mandatory.

questions.stem: Why is it important to record shielding gas cylinder change-outs and lot numbers on jobs performed under a CSA W47.1-certified WPS?

choices.A: For traceability so that if a weld fails inspection later, the gas lot and cylinder used can be linked to the weld
choices.B: For inventory tracking only
choices.C: Because the gas supplier requires it
choices.D: It is not required

questions.explanation: CSA W47.1 and W59 require traceability of consumables (filler metal lots, gas lots, fluxes) so that if a defect is later discovered, the root cause can be traced back to a specific batch of material. Inventory (B) and supplier requirements (C) are incidental. Traceability is a hard requirement, not optional (D).

questions.stem: According to CSA B354 (elevated work platforms), what is the maximum wind speed at which most self-propelled boom lifts may be operated outdoors, unless the manufacturer's rating is different?

choices.A: No wind speed limit if the platform is inside a barrier
choices.B: 22 m/s (49 mph)
choices.C: 5 m/s (11 mph)

questions.explanation: CSA B354 and most manufacturers set 12.5 m/s (approximately 28 mph or Beaufort 6) as the operating limit for outdoor use of self-propelled elevated work platforms unless the specific unit is rated differently. Always verify the load/wind chart posted in the platform. Answer B is above the tip-over threshold for most units; C is unnecessarily conservative; D ignores the wind loading on the platform occupants and materials.

sources.ref: Operation of elevated work platforms — wind speed limits

questions.stem: A welder needs to weld overhead beams 8 m off the shop floor. Which access equipment offers the best combination of stability, reach, and hot-work suitability?

choices.A: A single extension ladder
choices.B: A rope-and-harness rappel setup
choices.C: A stack of pallets and a step ladder
choices.D: A scissor lift or boom lift with a rated platform

questions.explanation: Elevated work platforms (scissor or boom) provide a stable working surface, guardrails, and a load rating for tools and materials — the correct choice for extended hot work at height. Ladders (A) are not stable enough for both hands to weld and violate most shop hot-work procedures. Pallet stacks (C) are prohibited. Rope access (B) is for specialized inspection, not welding.

questions.stem: Before using a scaffold to perform welding, what documentation should be checked?

choices.A: The manufacturer's original bill of sale
choices.B: The scaffold tag showing it has been inspected and released for use by a competent person
choices.C: The scaffold's paint colour
choices.D: No documentation is required

questions.explanation: CSA S269.2 and provincial OHS require scaffolds to be inspected by a competent person and tagged (green = released; yellow = restricted use; red = do not use). Welders must verify the tag before mounting. Purchase records (A), paint colour (C), and the no-check option (D) are all incorrect.

questions.stem: A rigger is preparing to lift a 3 m long, 500 kg steel plate using a two-leg wire-rope sling in a basket hitch. If the included angle between the sling legs at the hook is 60°, what is the load on each sling leg? (Ignore sling weight.)

choices.A: 250 kg
choices.B: 500 kg
choices.C: 289 kg

questions.explanation: Load per leg = (Total load ÷ 2) ÷ cos(θ/2), where θ is the included angle. = (500 ÷ 2) ÷ cos(30°) = 250 ÷ 0.866 ≈ 289 kg per leg. Answer A ignores sling angle. C treats each leg as carrying the full load. D doubles the load. ASME B30.9 tabulates these load factors.

sources.ref: Sling load calculations and angle factors

questions.stem: What is the correct hand signal for 'stop' when signalling a crane operator?

choices.A: Waving both hands overhead
choices.B: Both arms crossed above the head
choices.C: Thumb pointing up
choices.D: One arm extended horizontally, palm down, moved side-to-side

questions.explanation: ASME B30.5 standardizes crane signals. 'Stop' is one arm extended horizontally, palm down, moved back and forth. 'Emergency stop' is both arms extended horizontally, palms down, moved side-to-side. Crossed arms overhead (B) is not a standard signal. Thumb-up (C) means 'raise the load'.

questions.stem: Which shade of welding filter lens is generally recommended by CSA Z94.3 for SMAW at 100–200 amperes?

choices.A: Shade 11 or 12
choices.B: Shade 8
choices.C: Shade 5
choices.D: Shade 14

questions.explanation: CSA Z94.3 / ANSI Z87.1 recommend shade 10 for SMAW under 60 A, shade 11 for 60–160 A, and shade 12 for 160–250 A. Shade 5 (C) is oxy-fuel light cutting only. Shade 8 (B) is oxy-fuel heavy cutting. Shade 14 (D) is for very high-current processes or arc gouging above 500 A.

sources.ref: Industrial eye and face protection — welding filter shades

questions.stem: A welder is preparing to weld galvanized steel indoors. Which PPE and engineering control combination is required?

choices.A: Standard welding helmet only
choices.B: No additional PPE needed
choices.C: Welding helmet and a dust mask
choices.D: Welding helmet plus supplied-air respirator or approved P100 fume respirator, plus local exhaust ventilation

questions.explanation: Galvanized coatings produce zinc oxide fumes that cause metal fume fever and, at chronic exposure, more serious pulmonary effects. CSA W117.2 and provincial OHS require local exhaust ventilation and an approved respirator (supplied-air preferred, P100 minimum) whenever welding on galvanized or coated steel. A dust mask (C) does not filter metal fumes; standard helmet alone (A) or no PPE (B) exposes the welder.

sources.ref: Ventilation and respiratory protection for welding

questions.stem: A welder feels a mild sunburn-like sensation on the neck at the end of a long day of GTAW. What is the most likely cause and correct response?

choices.A: Skin allergy to filler metal — apply antihistamine
choices.B: Contact with hot metal — no action needed
choices.C: Heat exhaustion — take a break and drink water
choices.D: Arc flash burn from UV radiation exposure at the neck opening of the hood — cover exposed skin, add a bib or leather neck guard tomorrow

questions.explanation: GTAW produces high levels of UV radiation. Any exposed skin — neck, wrists, back of hands where gloves gap — burns like severe sunburn after hours of exposure. CSA W117.2 requires all exposed skin to be covered when arc welding. Skin allergy (A) presents as itching/rash, not burn. Heat exhaustion (C) has other symptoms. Hot metal contact (B) is a localized point burn, not diffuse redness.

sources.ref: UV radiation protection during arc welding

questions.stem: Under WHMIS 2015, which pictogram appears on a container of a compressed gas cylinder?

choices.A: Flame over circle
choices.B: Exploding bomb
choices.C: Gas cylinder pictogram (a cylinder in a circle)
choices.D: Corrosion pictogram

questions.explanation: WHMIS 2015 aligns with GHS. Compressed gases carry the 'gas cylinder' pictogram — a cylinder outline in a red-bordered diamond. Flame-over-circle (A) is oxidizers. Exploding bomb (B) is explosives or self-reactive substances. Corrosion (D) is corrosive substances. A single cylinder can carry multiple pictograms if it also poses those hazards (e.g. an oxidizing gas like O2 shows both gas cylinder and flame-over-circle).

questions.stem: Where should a Safety Data Sheet (SDS) for a filler metal used on the shop floor be kept, according to WHMIS 2015?

choices.A: Readily accessible to workers at or near the worksite (paper or electronic)
choices.B: Locked in the safety manager's office only
choices.C: Only at the supplier's warehouse
choices.D: Only on the SDS website

questions.explanation: WHMIS 2015 requires SDSs to be readily accessible to workers. This can be a binder near the shop, a computer terminal, or a scannable QR code — as long as workers can access it during their shift without barriers. Locked storage (B), off-site storage (C), or website-only (D) that requires internet access outside worker control do not meet the accessibility test.

questions.stem: Before entering a confined space to perform hot work, what atmospheric test values are typically required?

choices.A: Oxygen above 15%, any LEL is acceptable
choices.B: Oxygen between 19.5% and 23%, LEL below 10%, no toxics above OEL
choices.C: Only carbon monoxide needs to be tested
choices.D: No testing is required if PPE is worn

questions.explanation: CSA Z1006 and provincial OHS confined-space regulations require pre-entry atmospheric tests: O2 between 19.5% and 23% (below 19.5% is oxygen-deficient, above 23% is oxygen-enriched and a fire risk), LEL below 10% for hot work, and toxics below the applicable OEL. Continuous monitoring during work is also required.

sources.ref: Management of work in confined spaces

questions.stem: A welder is about to grind on a piece of steel that was previously used to store an unknown liquid. What is the correct pre-work step?

choices.A: Proceed — grinding is not a hot-work activity
choices.B: Weld a small test bead first to see what happens
choices.C: Fill the vessel with water and grind while wet
choices.D: Verify the contents of the previous liquid, ensure the vessel is emptied, cleaned, and vented per API 2015 or equivalent before any hot work

questions.explanation: Hot work (including grinding, which produces sparks and heat) on a vessel that held flammable or unknown liquids has caused multiple fatal explosions. API 2015 / OSHA / CSA W117.2 all require the vessel to be identified, emptied, cleaned, and either purged with inert gas or filled with water above the hot-work zone before any hot work. 'Grinding is not hot work' (A) is dangerously wrong — grinding sparks ignite vapours the same as welding.

sources.ref: Safe entry and cleaning of tanks

questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of a pre-job hazard assessment (also called Field Level Hazard Assessment or FLHA)?

choices.A: To assign blame after an incident
choices.B: To satisfy insurance paperwork only
choices.C: To identify hazards specific to the job and establish controls before work begins
choices.D: To track work hours

questions.explanation: FLHAs are a proactive safety tool — the crew identifies job-specific hazards (weather, proximity, tools, energies) and controls before starting. Blame assignment (A), insurance (B), and time tracking (D) are unrelated functions. Alberta OHS Code Part 2 requires hazard assessments.

questions.stem: A welder is given a WPS (Welding Procedure Specification) for a job. What is the first check to make before starting?

choices.A: Confirm the WPS was signed by the welding engineer
choices.B: Confirm the WPS covers the base metal, thickness, process, filler, position, and joint design that match this job
choices.C: Ignore the WPS and use personal preference
choices.D: Check the paper quality of the WPS

questions.explanation: A WPS is only valid for the ranges of variables it specifies. Before using it, confirm the base metal (P-number), thickness range, process (SMAW/GTAW/etc), filler classification (F/A-number), position, and joint design all match the job. If any variable is outside the WPS range, a new procedure is required. Signature (A) is important but secondary to fit-for-purpose. C is unsafe. D is trivial.

questions.stem: What is meant by 'housekeeping' in a welding shop context?

choices.A: Keeping the work area free of trip hazards, combustibles, and cable tangles, with tools returned to storage
choices.B: Cleaning the office
choices.C: Painting the walls
choices.D: Restocking the vending machine

questions.explanation: Shop housekeeping directly affects safety and productivity: trip hazards cause falls, combustibles cause fires, cable tangles cause pinch and pull injuries, and lost tools waste time. CSA W117.2 and OHS codes require welding areas to be kept clear.

questions.stem: A welder finishes a job and disconnects the SMAW electrode from the holder. What should happen to the electrode stub?

choices.A: Place it in a designated stub container so it does not become a slip/trip/burn hazard and can be recycled
choices.B: Drop it on the floor — the next crew will sweep
choices.C: Kick it under the workbench
choices.D: Store it in a pocket for the next job

questions.explanation: Hot electrode stubs on the floor are trip hazards and can cause burn injuries or ignite combustibles. Designated stub containers keep the area safe and allow scrap collection. Options A, C, and D all leave the hazard uncontrolled. Good housekeeping is called out in most WHMIS-adjacent shop procedures.

questions.stem: What is the correct storage temperature range for low-hydrogen SMAW electrodes (e.g. E7018) once they are removed from the sealed original container?

choices.A: Room temperature
choices.B: Rod oven at approximately 120°C (250°F)
choices.C: Refrigerated at 4°C
choices.D: Freezer at -18°C

questions.explanation: Low-hydrogen electrodes must be stored in a heated rod oven at approximately 120°C (250°F) once opened to prevent moisture pickup in the flux coating. Moisture becomes hydrogen in the arc, which causes hydrogen-induced cracking. AWS A5.1 and manufacturer data specify the temperature. Room-temperature (A) exposure is limited to a few hours. Cold storage (C, D) actually promotes condensation.

questions.stem: A welder receives a new bulk container of ER70S-6 GMAW wire. Which handling practice is correct?

choices.A: Keep the wire in its sealed packaging until installed, keep spools covered when not in use, and store in a dry area
choices.B: Leave the wire uncovered in the shop to acclimate
choices.C: Wipe the wire with cutting oil before use
choices.D: Freeze the wire before use

questions.explanation: Solid GMAW wire is copper-coated for conductivity and corrosion resistance. Exposure to shop air, moisture, or oils causes surface contamination that leads to porosity and feed problems. Keep sealed until use, cover between uses, store dry. Oil (C) contaminates. Freezing (D) causes condensation.

questions.stem: Under CSA W47.1, what is a 'tack weld'?

choices.A: The final finish pass on a groove weld
choices.B: A weld made without filler metal
choices.C: Any weld under 6 mm long
choices.D: A small, temporary or permanent weld used to hold parts in alignment during subsequent welding

questions.explanation: A tack weld holds parts in place while the joint is welded. It may be consumed by later passes (temporary) or left in place and incorporated into the final weld (permanent, in which case it must meet the same quality as the joint). CSA W59 clause 5.5 covers tack weld requirements — size, quality, and inspection.

questions.stem: When performing setup for a groove weld on 12 mm plate, what is a reasonable maximum tack weld spacing?

choices.A: 50 mm
choices.B: One tack at each end only
choices.C: Approximately 150–300 mm depending on plate size and stiffness
choices.D: 1 metre

questions.explanation: Practical tack spacing on 12 mm plate is typically 150–300 mm, closer on thinner material or where distortion is a concern, farther on stiff assemblies. Very close tacks (A, 50 mm) waste time and may overheat. End-only tacks (B) cause bowing during welding. 1 m spacing (D) is too far and allows the joint to open. WPS documents typically specify.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of preheat applied before welding thick carbon steel sections?

choices.A: To burn off surface paint
choices.B: To slow the cooling rate of the weld and HAZ, reducing hardness and hydrogen retention
choices.C: To make the metal easier to cut
choices.D: To expand the metal so the joint is easier to fit

questions.explanation: Preheat serves three linked purposes: (1) reduces the cooling rate, which reduces peak hardness of the HAZ; (2) allows hydrogen to diffuse out of the weld before it cools; (3) reduces thermal shock and residual stress. Preheat temperatures come from CSA W59 Annex E or AWS D1.1 Annex I based on carbon-equivalent, thickness, and process. Paint burning (A) is a side effect, not the purpose.

questions.stem: A WPS specifies preheat of 100°C minimum and maximum interpass of 250°C. During welding, the welder measures the interpass temperature as 280°C. What is the correct action?

choices.A: Stop welding, allow the joint to cool below 250°C, then continue
choices.B: Continue welding — 30°C over is acceptable
choices.C: Increase amperage to compensate
choices.D: Reduce preheat to 80°C to offset

questions.explanation: Maximum interpass temperature is an essential WPS variable. Exceeding it can cause excessive grain growth, reduced toughness, and, in quenched-and-tempered steels, loss of mechanical properties. The correct response is to stop, let the joint cool below the specified max, then resume. Ignoring the limit (B), changing parameters (C), or reducing preheat (D) all deviate from the qualified WPS.

questions.stem: What is a 'stringer bead'?

choices.A: A bead deposited with a side-to-side weaving motion
choices.B: A narrow bead deposited without significant side-to-side motion, following a straight travel path
choices.C: A bead used only in overhead position
choices.D: The first pass in any multi-pass weld

questions.explanation: A stringer bead is a narrow bead deposited with little or no oscillation. Weave beads (A) use lateral motion. Stringers give lower heat input per pass and are preferred for many code-compliant welds on high-strength steels and stainless. First-pass (D) usage is called a root pass, not stringer.

questions.stem: A CSA W47.1 shop is running a job. Who is authorized to sign the final weld inspection report?

choices.A: Any welder in the shop
choices.B: The client's project manager
choices.C: The shop apprentice
choices.D: The Welding Engineer or a CWB-certified inspector as required by the QA/QC program

questions.explanation: CSA W47.1 Division 1/2 shops require a Welding Engineer, and inspection is performed by CWB-certified inspectors (Level 1, 2, or 3 as appropriate). The QA/QC program defines exact sign-off authority. Welders (A, C) can perform in-process visual checks but are not the inspection authority. The client (B) may review the report but does not issue it.

sources.ref: Certification of welding inspectors and inspection organizations

questions.stem: What must a welder record when performing production welding under a CSA W47.1 program?

choices.A: Nothing — the WPS is enough
choices.B: Only the number of electrodes used
choices.C: Weld ID, welder ID/stamp, WPS reference, date, and any deviations from the WPS
choices.D: Only the total welding time

questions.explanation: Weld tracking under a certified program requires enough information to trace each weld back to who made it, when, and under which procedure. This is essential for both quality control and for corrective action if a weld fails inspection later. Consumable count (B) and time (D) alone are insufficient.

questions.stem: A welder notices during a job that the WPS calls for E7018 with 25 mm A516 Gr 70, but the shop only stocks E7018-1 H4R electrodes in that diameter. What is the correct action?

choices.A: Use E7018-1 H4R without checking — it's stronger, so it's fine
choices.B: Substitute a GMAW wire
choices.C: Check with the welding supervisor and confirm whether E7018-1 H4R is acceptable under the qualified WPS or whether a supplementary essential variable change requires re-qualification
choices.D: Skip the job

questions.explanation: Filler metal classification is an essential variable in most codes. E7018-1 H4R has additional impact toughness and diffusible hydrogen requirements beyond plain E7018 — often it can substitute freely, but this depends on the WPS and code. The right move is always to check with the welding supervisor rather than assume. Blind substitution (A) or process change (B) can invalidate qualification and expose the shop to liability. Skipping (D) doesn't solve the problem.

sources.ref: Essential variables and filler metal substitution

questions.stem: For a synthetic (nylon or polyester) web sling in a vertical hitch, the working load limit (WLL) marked on the tag is the maximum load for which configuration?

choices.A: Choker hitch at any angle
choices.B: Basket hitch with legs parallel
choices.C: Vertical hitch only
choices.D: All hitches at any angle

questions.explanation: ASME B30.9 requires sling tags to show WLL for the three main configurations: vertical, basket, and choker. The vertical rating is the base. Basket hitch with parallel legs is typically 2× vertical; choker hitch is typically ~0.75× vertical. Loading at an angle further reduces capacity.

questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of a fire watch during and after hot work in areas where combustibles cannot be moved more than 11 m away?

choices.A: To watch the welder for safe technique
choices.B: To supervise the apprentice
choices.C: To detect and extinguish spot fires or smoldering material that may ignite during or after welding — typically maintained for at least 30–60 min after hot work stops
choices.D: To count electrodes used

questions.explanation: NFPA 51B and CSA W117.2 require a fire watch when hot work is performed within 11 m of combustibles that cannot be removed. The fire watch has extinguishing means at hand and maintains watch during work and for 30 minutes (NFPA baseline; some jurisdictions 60 min) after work ends to catch delayed ignition from smoldering material.

sources.ref: Fire prevention during welding, cutting, and other hot work

questions.stem: During job planning, which sequence best represents a proper hazard control hierarchy from most to least effective?

choices.A: Elimination → substitution → engineering controls → administrative controls → PPE
choices.B: PPE → administrative controls → engineering controls → substitution → elimination
choices.C: Administrative controls → PPE → engineering controls → elimination → substitution
choices.D: Substitution → PPE → elimination → engineering controls → administrative controls

questions.explanation: The hierarchy of controls (CSA Z1000, NIOSH) ranks elimination first (remove the hazard entirely), then substitution (replace with something safer), then engineering controls (isolate people from the hazard), then administrative controls (procedures, training), and PPE last as the final barrier. PPE is the least effective because it depends entirely on the worker wearing it correctly at all times.

sources.ref: Occupational health and safety management — hierarchy of controls

questions.stem: A welder's work area contains a gas cylinder cart with oxygen and acetylene cylinders. What is the minimum separation required between the cylinders in storage if they cannot be moved?

choices.A: 6.1 m (20 ft) apart, or separated by a non-combustible barrier at least 1.5 m (5 ft) high with a fire rating of at least 30 min
choices.B: No separation required if they are in a cart
choices.C: 1 m separation is always enough
choices.D: Only separation between full and empty cylinders is required

questions.explanation: CSA Z94.7 / NFPA 55 / CGA P-1 require oxygen and fuel-gas cylinders in storage to be either 6.1 m apart or separated by a 1.5 m high non-combustible barrier with 30-min fire rating. This prevents a fuel-gas leak from being ignited by oxygen enrichment (or vice versa). Cylinders in active use on a cart are exempt while in use but must be properly separated when stored.

questions.stem: Which technique is generally required for welding austenitic stainless steel to minimize sensitization?

choices.A: Weave beads with high heat input
choices.B: Post-weld heat treatment at 800°C for all welds
choices.C: Preheat above 200°C
choices.D: Stringer beads with controlled low heat input and interpass temperature typically ≤ 175°C

questions.explanation: Austenitic stainless steels (300-series) are prone to chromium-carbide precipitation (sensitization) if held in the 450–870°C range too long. Stringer beads and controlled low heat input, with interpass typically limited to 175°C or lower, keep the HAZ out of that range as much as possible. Weave beads (A) and high preheat (C) increase time-at-temperature. PWHT at 800°C (B) is exactly the sensitization range and is not standard for austenitic SS.

questions.stem: A CWB-certified inspector rejects a weld for excessive porosity. The welder's stamp is on the joint. What is the typical first step in a shop CAR (corrective action request)?

choices.A: Fire the welder
choices.B: Investigate root cause — check consumables lot, gas flow, technique, WPS compliance, base metal condition — and record findings before deciding on rework and preventive action
choices.C: Re-weld the joint immediately without investigation
choices.D: Ignore the defect and ship

questions.explanation: CSA W47.1 and ISO 9001 require corrective action to address root cause, not symptoms. Porosity has many possible causes (moisture, contamination, gas coverage, technique) and jumping to rework (C) without understanding cause means the defect will recur. Firing the welder (A) is neither corrective nor lawful without investigation. Ignoring the defect (D) is fraud and a safety liability.
